title: Solvang, California
seoTitle: Charter Bus to Solvang, California: Group Trip Guide
excerpt: A charter bus to Solvang gives a group the Danish village and the Santa Ynez wineries in one day, with nobody driving. Stops, vehicle sizing and timing.

heroImage.alt: Half-timbered buildings and a wooden windmill on the main street of Solvang, California

extraImage.alt: A bakery window in Solvang displaying Danish pastries and aebleskiver

body.text: Solvang was founded by Danish immigrants in 1911 and has committed to it ever since: windmills, half-timbered facades, bakeries selling æbleskiver by the dozen. It is also the front door to the Santa Ynez Valley wine region, which is the reason most groups come. A charter bus to Solvang lets you have both in one day, which is difficult to arrange any other way once tasting is involved.
The town is walkable, which changes the plan

Solvang's center is about four blocks square and entirely walkable. That is unusual for a group destination and it simplifies the day enormously — the bus parks once, the group disperses, and everybody meets back at the same corner. No shuttling between attractions, no one getting lost.
Two or three hours is right for the town itself. Longer than that and a group has seen the shops twice.
What to do in the village

items: The bakeries. Æbleskiver, Danish pastries and butter cookies, and the queue at the best of them is part of the experience.
Elverhøj Museum of History and Art: the story of the Danish settlement, in a house built in the Danish provincial style. Half an hour, and it makes sense of everything outside.
The Hans Christian Andersen Museum: small, free and charming, above the bookshop.
The windmills and the Little Mermaid replica: the photographs the group came for, all within a few minutes' walk.
Old Mission Santa Inés, on the eastern edge of town: one of the California missions, founded 1804, and a genuinely quiet twenty minutes.

body.text: The wineries are the other half of the day

The Santa Ynez Valley surrounds Solvang, with tasting rooms in Los Olivos, Buellton and Santa Ynez and vineyards scattered along the valley roads. Most are within twenty minutes of the village. This is the part of the day that makes a charter genuinely necessary rather than merely convenient — a tasting itinerary in separate cars means somebody is not participating.

Two wineries plus the village is a comfortable day. Three is possible if the group is efficient and the tastings are standing rather than seated. Book the tasting rooms in advance for any group over about eight; the smaller producers will otherwise be full.
Which charter bus suits a Solvang day

items: Twenty to thirty-two: a [mini bus](/fleet/mini-buses) is the standard vehicle for valley wine days, fitting winery driveways that a full coach cannot.
Forty to fifty-six: a full-size [charter bus](/fleet/charter-buses) works well for a club outing or a corporate group coming from Los Angeles, with an on-board restroom for the drive up.
A celebration: a [party bus](/fleet/party-buses) for 14 to 40 suits a birthday or bachelorette group moving between tasting rooms.
Ten to fourteen: a [sprinter van](/fleet/sprinter-vans) reaches the smallest producers and parks anywhere in the village.

body.text: From [Santa Barbara](/locations/california/santa-barbara) it is about forty-five minutes over the San Marcos Pass, which is a scenic road in its own right. From Los Angeles allow two and a half to three hours depending on traffic through Ventura, and from San Luis Obispo around an hour. Solvang is also a natural inland detour off the Pacific Coast Highway, which is how a lot of groups first encounter it.

Coach parking sits on the edge of the village rather than in the middle of it, which is exactly what you want — the vehicle waits somewhere sensible while the group walks. Groups searching for charter bus rental near me for a wine country day should give the pickup point as well as the destination when they ask for a price, because starting from [Santa Barbara](/locations/california/santa-barbara) rather than Los Angeles typically buys an extra tasting room.

The valley is pleasant year-round, which is one of its advantages. Spring brings wildflowers and mild weather, autumn brings harvest and the busiest tasting rooms, and winter is quiet enough that the village feels like a town rather than a destination. Summer is warm inland and the village is at its most crowded on weekends — a weekday visit in July is a substantially better experience than a Saturday one.

A note on scheduling the tasting rooms. Most Santa Ynez producers close by five, which is earlier than groups arriving from Los Angeles tend to expect. If your drive up is three hours and you want two wineries plus the village, the departure time is not negotiable — it is eight in the morning, and building the day backwards from the last tasting slot is the only way to make it fit.

Groups that would rather not start that early should consider staying overnight in the valley. Solvang has plenty of lodging, the village is a pleasant place to spend an evening, and a two-day trip removes the drive from both ends of the tasting day.
